title: Lesson 2.2 Knowledge Check
description: Five questions on beats, variables, and AI voice in avatar performance. Unlimited attempts; your best score counts.

questions.text: In script scoring, a new beat begins when:
questions.feedback: Beats mark shifts in tactic: from pleading to threatening, from remembering to deciding.

questions.text: Which are the four variables you control per beat in most animation tools? Select all that apply.
questions.feedback: Gesture, expression, camera, and voice. Together they are the abstraction of a performance into controllable variables.

questions.text: A completed beat sheet that lists the gesture, expression, camera, and voice for each beat in order is an example of algorithm design.
questions.feedback: It is an ordered set of instructions the tool carries out; that is algorithm design.

questions.text: Why does this lesson require you to record your own voice for at least one beat?
options: AI voices are not allowed in the course
To compare synthetic delivery with a human tactic-driven delivery and evaluate the difference
Because Animaker does not offer text-to-speech
questions.feedback: Default AI delivery is even and dramatically empty. Comparing it with your own delivery is AI feedback evaluation applied to performance.

questions.text: What is the best way to give peer feedback on an avatar performance in this lesson?
options: Watch with the creator's beat sheet beside you and note where the performance matched or drifted from the plan
questions.feedback: Co-review against the shared plan is the collaboration competency in practice.
